history.titleZh: 开发者利用GPT-6 Astra在《我的世界》中原生运行《使命召唤：黑色行动2》 Hijacked地图——借助Minecraft的OpenGL环境实现45fps性能
history.descriptionZh:
AI 与游戏开发爱好者 Luckey Faraday 近日展示了一项引人注目的技术成果：将 2012 年《使命召唤：黑色行动 2》中的 Hijacked 游艇地图以“原生”方式运行在《Minecraft》中。这里的“原生”并非通过浏览器、也不是在《Minecraft》世界里放一块虚拟屏幕来显示，而是让该地图及其游戏逻辑直接运行在《Minecraft》自身的 OpenGL 上下文中。视频显示，这张经典 FPS 地图能够全屏运行，帧率约为 45 fps，整体表现相当流畅，已经具备可玩性。

根据 Faraday 在 X/Twitter 上的说明，这一项目经历了几个阶段。最初，他制作了一个基于浏览器的《黑色行动 2》移植版本；随后，这个版本被“塞进”《Minecraft》，但当时只能在游戏内的一台虚拟 PC 屏幕上运行，本质上仍是一个嵌套的独立游戏窗口。之后，Faraday 让 GPT Astra 参与重建整个项目，将 Hijacked 地图及相关内容用 Java 重写，使其能够直接接入《Minecraft》的 OpenGL 渲染环境。最终，地图、碰撞检测、机器人、导航网格、武器和渲染等模块全部作为 Fabric mod 在《Minecraft》内部运行。

技术核心在于 Fabric。Fabric 是《Minecraft》Java 版的一个轻量级、开源 mod 加载器和开发 API，允许开发者向游戏中注入自定义内容、逻辑和渲染代码。Faraday 通过 Fabric 框架，把《黑色行动 2》的 Hijacked 地图和游戏元素直接集成进《Minecraft》，而不是让它们运行在外部模拟器或独立进程中。换句话说，玩家看到的不再是“游戏中播放另一个游戏”，而是《Minecraft》引擎本身在渲染和承载这张 FPS 地图。这也是该项目被称为“原生运行”的关键原因。

从性能参数看，目前公开的视频展示的是全屏约 45 fps 的效果。原文没有披露测试硬件、分辨率或具体优化细节，但对于一个将完整 FPS 地图、碰撞、AI 机器人、导航网格和武器系统移植进《Minecraft》的项目而言，45 fps 已足以证明其可玩性和技术可行性。与此前只能在游戏内虚拟屏幕上显示的版本相比，新版本在集成度、渲染路径和交互体验上都有明显跃升。

这一项目的创新点不仅在于跨游戏引擎的内容移植，更在于 AI 智能体参与代码重建的方式。Faraday 运营着一个 AI 开发者社区，鼓励同好协作构建演示、分享日志和代码。此次 Hijacked 地图的移植正是该流程的典型案例：先做浏览器可玩版本，再塞入《Minecraft》作为屏幕内游戏，最后借助 GPT Astra 用 Java 重写并接入《Minecraft》OpenGL 环境。这说明 AI 编程模型已经能够参与复杂项目的重构和平台适配，尽管仍需要人类开发者设定目标、验证结果和继续完善。

从影响和应用场景看，这类实验展示了 AI 辅助游戏移植、复古游戏复刻和 mod 开发的潜力。开发者未来或可利用类似流程，将旧游戏、旧地图或独立项目快速迁移到新平台，降低人工重写成本。同时，《Minecraft》作为史上最畅销、开放性与扩展性极强的沙盒游戏，一直是技术实验的温床。此前社区曾把 500 万参数的 ChatGPT 模型 CraftGPT 塞进游戏，也有玩家用 44.5 万个命令方块在原版《Minecraft》中构建 AI 聊天机器人，以及 GPT-6 Astra 模型自主完成《Portal》等案例。Faraday 表示，目前项目“还有大量工作要做”，但 Hijacked 游艇地图已经能在《Minecraft》中较流畅地运行；如果继续推进，下一步可能加入更多地图、更多武器和多人模式。这不仅是游戏 mod 的炫技，也反映了 AI 辅助编程与开放游戏平台结合后，可能催生更高效的跨平台内容重建方式。

history.title: Apple eyes Nvidia NVLink to power its new custom M8 Ultra AI servers — historically bitter rivals reportedly team up for 2029 data center push
history.description: Apple is reportedly interested in using Nvidia's NVLink Fusion for its own data center platforms.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Apple is reportedly developing AI servers based on its own M-series processors and is evaluating NVLink Fusion technology for interconnects, according to The Information. The machines are expected to use M8 Ultra processors and arrive in 2029, the report claims. For now, the usage of the NVLink Fusion platform is not formalized and has not been confirmed by either Apple or Nvidia, but if Apple decides to use it instead of competing solutions, this may have significantly broader market implications than just Apple using Nvidia hardware.Apple looking for fast interconnectsApple is reportedly considering at least two server configurations: a smaller machine equipped with two M8 Ultra processors and a higher-end version featuring four M8 Ultra system-on-chips. Although Apple has its own UltraFusion technology for stitching two high-end SoCs together seamlessly, it looks like the company does not have a proper solution for scale-up and scale-out connectivity of its processors, which is where Nvidia's NVLink Fusion comes into play. Apparently, Apple wants to use NVLink infrastructure, which includes not only an interconnection protocol, but also switches, chiplets that add NVLink connectivity, and a software stack, for its servers. The project was reportedly initiated around a year ago and was backed by John Ternus while he headed Apple's hardware engineering organization.Apple already builds custom servers for Private Cloud Compute, which handle AI workloads too demanding for local execution on iPhones and Macs, The Information claims. Most of these machines use Apple's internally developed connectivity technologies, which are reportedly too slow and costly for large-scale commercial deployments, which is why Apple is looking elsewhere.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: More than NVLink?The Information specifically mentions Apple's need for connectivity technology suitable for large-scale deployments, although it does not explain exactly what this means architecturally. If the publication is referring to connecting multiple servers into larger clusters, this would normally be the job of scale-out technologies such as Ethernet or InfiniBand, rather than a scale-up fabric such as NVLink. Nvidia originally developed its NVLink fabric technology to scale-up performance of its accelerators, so the technology is optimized for accelerator-to-accelerator connectivity and enables a rack of Nvidia GPUs to function as a tightly coupled compute domain. There is a different implementation called NVLink-C2C, which is a coherent chip-to-chip interface for connecting CPUs to accelerators and CPUs to CPUsMeanwhile, modern Apple M Pro and M Ultra processors are system-in-packages consisting of a CPU chiplet and a GPU/neural engine chiplet, which are stitched together using TSMC's SoIC-mH technology. If Apple continues to use this architecture (very likely), an M8 Ultra processor can be considered as a CPU and an accelerator. However, this raises the question of how Apple intends to connect M8 Ultra processors to NVLink and which components of the SiP would participate in the NVLink domain. One possibility is that Apple could expose the accelerator portion of M8 Ultra to NVLink through an NVLink Fusion chiplet, which effectively means it will treat it as an accelerator for a scale-up domain. Another possibility is that Apple is developing a different accelerator architecture for its servers, perhaps by simply placing the GPU/NPU chiplet onto a separate substrate/interposer and equipping it with its own memory, though there is currently no evidence that confirms such a design for a chip that is years away. You may like Apple's rumored M7 Ultra targets 1.5TB of memory and Blackwell-class AI performance, report claims Google could build more AI accelerators than Nvidia sells in 2028, analyst claims Apple will skip its high-end M6 Mac chips and fast-track an AI-focused M7 generation for 2027, report claims Another thing to keep in mind is that Apple is a member of the UALink Consortium, an organization overseeing development of industry-standard UALink accelerator-to-accelerator interconnections that supports up to 1,024 accelerators. While for now there is a limited choice of UALink switches, by 2029, there will be industry-standard switches offering different performance and capabilities, which makes the choice of NVLink as a scale-up fabric even stranger.One possible explanation is that Apple is interested in considerably more than NVLink itself. NVLink Fusion is part of Nvidia's rack-scale and data center infrastructure architecture, which can combine NVLink scale-up connectivity with Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet or Quantum-X InfiniBand scale-out networks, including switches equipped with co-packaged optics. Thus, Apple could potentially adopt Nvidia technology for both scale-up and scale-out connectivity instead of developing an entire data center networking stack of its own. This is merely speculation for now, but such an approach would effectively mean that Apple is building AI servers around significant portions of Nvidia's data center architecture while retaining its own processors and not using Nvidia accelerators. If this happens, this will be a testament that Nvidia is now setting de facto standards for AI data centers, no matter which AI accelerators and CPUs are used.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsBurying the hatchet?Without a doubt, Nvidia is a leading supplier of data center hardware, so it is logical for Apple to work with the company if the two companies are indeed working together on Apple's data center platform.Apple and Nvidia are not exactly good partners. The feud between the two companies began in the early 2000s, when Steve Jobs accused Nvidia of infringing on Pixar's patents on which Nvidia responded that it owned more graphics IP than Pixar and therefore could sue the company. Later on, Apple and Nvidia had disagreements over GPU design decisions that the latter supplied to the former. However, then came 'Bumpgate' as Nvidia supplied Apple and other PC makers defective GPUs in 2007 – 2008, did not acknowledge the problem, and then resisted fully compensating Apple and other PC makers for their repair costs, which is when the relationship between the companies got especially dire. Apple continued to use Nvidia GPUs till 2014 or 2015, at which point it switched to AMD's Radeon, and then abandoned discrete third-party GPUs altogether.More recently, Apple started to use Nvidia's hardware again. The latest Siri AI is primarily powered by Apple Foundation Models developed in collaboration with Google using Gemini technology. Server-side inference runs through Apple's Private Cloud Compute architecture, and many of the workloads are hosted on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in Google Cloud. Yet, using Nvidia hardware in the cloud and adopting the company's technologies for your own platforms is a completely different thing. history.titleZh: 苹果瞄准英伟达NVLink，为其全新定制M8 Ultra AI服务器提供动力——据报道，这对宿敌联手推动2029年数据中心布局
history.descriptionZh:
据 The Information 报道，苹果正在开发基于自研 M 系列处理器的 AI 服务器，并评估英伟达的 NVLink Fusion 互连技术。这些机器预计采用 M8 Ultra 处理器，2029 年推出。报道称，苹果至少考虑两种配置：配备两个 M8 Ultra 处理器的较小机器，以及配备四个 M8 Ultra 系统级芯片的高端版本。目前 NVLink Fusion 平台的使用尚未正式确定，苹果和英伟达均未确认。如果苹果决定采用该技术而非竞争方案，其市场影响可能远不止苹果使用英伟达硬件。

背景方面，苹果已为 Private Cloud Compute 构建定制服务器，处理 iPhone 和 Mac 本地难以执行的 AI 工作负载。这些机器大多采用苹果内部开发的连接技术，但据称对于大规模商业部署而言太慢且成本太高，因此苹果寻求外部方案。该项目约一年前启动，得到当时领导苹果硬件工程的 John Ternus 支持。苹果拥有 UltraFusion 技术，可无缝拼接两个高端 SoC，但似乎缺乏处理器 scale-up 和 scale-out 连接的完整方案，这正是 NVLink Fusion 可能介入的地方。

核心技术方面，NVLink Fusion 是英伟达机架规模和数据中心基础设施架构的一部分，包含互连协议、交换机、添加 NVLink 连接的 chiplet 以及软件栈。英伟达最初开发 NVLink 用于加速器 scale-up，优化加速器到加速器连接，使一机架 GPU 作为紧耦合计算域运行。另有 NVLink-C2C，是用于 CPU 到加速器和 CPU 到 CPU 的一致性芯片到芯片接口。现代苹果 M Pro 和 M Ultra 是系统级封装，由 CPU chiplet 和 GPU/神经引擎 chiplet 通过台积电 SoIC-mH 技术拼接。若延续该架构，M8 Ultra 可视为 CPU 与加速器。苹果如何将 M8 Ultra 连接到 NVLink 尚不明确：可能通过 NVLink Fusion chiplet 将加速器部分暴露给 NVLink，将其视为 scale-up 域中的加速器；也可能为服务器开发不同加速器架构。目前无证据确认。

对比与疑问方面，苹果是 UALink 联盟成员，该联盟推动行业标准 UALink 加速器互连，支持最多 1024 个加速器。目前 UALink 交换机选择有限，但到 2029 年将有不同性能和能力的行业标准交换机。因此选择 NVLink 作为 scale-up 结构更显奇怪。一种解释是苹果感兴趣的不只是 NVLink，而是英伟达完整的数据中心架构：NVLink Fusion 可与英伟达 Spectrum-X 以太网或 Quantum-X InfiniBand scale-out 网络结合，包括共封装光学交换机。苹果可能采用英伟达技术进行 scale-up 和 scale-out 连接，而非自研整个数据中心网络栈。目前仅为推测，但若成真，意味着苹果围绕英伟达数据中心架构的重要部分构建 AI 服务器，同时保留自己的处理器，不使用英伟达加速器。这将证明英伟达正在为 AI 数据中心设定事实标准，无论使用何种 AI 加速器和 CPU。

历史背景上，苹果与英伟达关系并不好。恩怨始于 2000 年代初，史蒂夫·乔布斯指控英伟达侵犯 Pixar 专利，英伟达回应称其拥有更多图形 IP。后双方在 GPU 设计决策上分歧。2007 至 2008 年“Bumpgate”事件中，英伟达向苹果等 PC 厂商供应缺陷 GPU，未承认问题并抗拒全额补偿维修成本，关系尤其恶化。苹果继续使用英伟达 GPU 至 2014 或 2015 年，后转向 AMD Radeon，最终放弃第三方独显。最近苹果又开始使用英伟达硬件：最新 Siri AI 主要由苹果与谷歌合作使用 Gemini 技术开发的 Apple Foundation Models 驱动。服务器端推理通过苹果 Private Cloud Compute 架构，许多工作负载托管在 Google Cloud 的英伟达 Blackwell GPU 上。然而，在云中使用英伟达硬件与采用其技术用于自家平台完全不同。

技术影响与应用场景方面，若苹果采用 NVLink Fusion，将用于其 AI 服务器，可能支持 Private Cloud Compute 的大规模 AI 推理和训练。M8 Ultra 预计 2029 年问世，结合两个或四个 SoC，可提供更高计算密度。NVLink Fusion 可让苹果将自研芯片组成紧耦合域，并通过英伟达网络扩展。应用场景包括 Siri 等 AI 服务、Apple Intelligence 云端推理以及未来更复杂的基础模型。技术影响在于，英伟达可能从芯片供应商进一步成为 AI 数据中心互连和网络标准制定者，即使客户使用自研加速器也依赖其架构。这对其生态是重大扩展。同时，苹果选择 NVLink 而非 UALink 也可能影响 UALink 生态发展。目前均为传闻，细节未确认，需要等待官方消息。

history.content: Snap is introducing “Specs Intelligence,” a new AI assistant that can connect other digital accounts to help you with things like work tasks and keeping track of travel information. It seems similar to AI assistants like Meta’s Muse and Gemini’s Spark, though Snap is pitching Specs Intelligence as an “anticipatory AI service” that “helps you manage what needs attention today, so you can make progress toward your longer-term goals.” Like with other AI assistants, you can also chat with it.Specs Intelligence is being launched alongside Specs, Snap’s first consumer pair of augmented reality glasses. But it’s also available on iOS today in preview, and you can get on a waitlist for the “full early-access experience” that’s coming to Mac. Snap wouldn’t say on the record how the preview differs from the full experience.Here’s how Specs Intelligence works, according to Snap:SPECS Intelligence builds an understanding of your goals, priorities, relationships, and routines from the apps and tools you choose to connect. The service is designed to carry that personal context across devices and deepens its understanding over time, helping you move between work, personal responsibilities, and the things you care about.SPECS Intelligence is designed to anticipate when help would be useful and surface relevant information and actions without waiting for a prompt. Before a meeting, it could highlight decisions to make, questions to ask, and things to remember. For an upcoming trip, it could bring together flight, hotel, and dinner plans while flagging a work deadline that falls during the visit.If you’re using Specs Intelligence on the Specs AR glasses, Specs can pull personal content and place it “directly into view” when relevant, like when you ask for a daily briefing before work. According to a video, Specs Intelligence can connect to apps like Gmail and Slack.Specs Intelligence uses “a proprietary combination of open-source models hosted in the US alongside local LLMs,” according to spokesperson Cassie Bumgarner, who adds that “We regularly update the mixture of models as we continue iterating towards the best version of SPECS Intelligence.” But the company faces real challenges in that it needs users to trust it with their information and with data from connected services. Snap is trying to get ahead of those concerns by saying that it can’t view or access personal content you use with Specs Intelligence and that “Personal content from connected accounts will not be used to train or fine-tune Snap’s AI models, or to serve personalized ads.” But it’s still a tall order, especially given how we’ve found other AI assistants with broad access to data to be pretty unnerving.

history.titleZh: Snap推出全新Specs AI工具，即将登陆iOS和Mac平台
history.descriptionZh:
Snap 正在推出名为 “Specs Intelligence” 的新 AI 助手，它可以连接用户的其他数字账户，帮助处理工作任务、跟踪旅行信息等。从定位看，它类似 Meta 的 Muse 和 Gemini 的 Spark，但 Snap 将其包装为一种“预判式 AI 服务”，强调它不只是等待用户提问，而是主动帮助用户管理当天需要关注的事项，从而推动长期目标。用户也可以像使用其他 AI 助手一样与它聊天。

Specs Intelligence 与 Snap 首款消费级增强现实眼镜 Specs 一同发布，但它并非只服务于 AR 硬件。该服务当天已在 iOS 上以预览形式提供，用户还可以加入等待名单，以获得即将登陆 Mac 的“完整早期体验”。不过，Snap 不愿公开说明预览版与完整版之间究竟有哪些差异。

按照 Snap 的描述，Specs Intelligence 会根据用户主动连接的应用和工具，逐步理解用户的目标、优先级、人际关系和日常习惯。它被设计为能够跨设备携带这些个人上下文，并随时间加深理解，帮助用户在工作、个人责任和真正关心的事情之间切换。其核心创新在于“预判”：系统会在不需要用户输入提示的情况下，判断何时提供帮助有用，并主动呈现相关信息和可执行动作。例如，在会议前，它可以突出需要做出的决定、应该提出的问题和需要记住的事项；在即将旅行时，它可以汇总航班、酒店和晚餐计划，同时标记旅行期间撞期的工作截止日期。如果用户在 Specs AR 眼镜上使用该服务，Specs 还能把个人内容在相关时刻“直接放入视野”，比如上班前请求每日简报。根据演示视频，Specs Intelligence 可以连接 Gmail 和 Slack 等应用。

技术架构方面，Snap 发言人 Cassie Bumgarner 表示，Specs Intelligence 使用了“一种专有组合：在美国托管的开源模型，加上本地 LLM”。她还称，随着团队持续迭代，Snap 会定期更新模型组合，以追求 Specs Intelligence 的最佳版本。本地 LLM 的引入意味着部分推理或上下文理解可能在设备侧完成，但原文并未披露具体模型规模、芯片平台、算力需求、推理延迟、准确率或任何基准测试数据。因此，无法对 Specs Intelligence 的性能进行量化评估。与竞品的对比也主要停留在功能定位层面：它被拿来与 Meta 的 Muse、Gemini 的 Spark 类比，但 Snap 强调自身是更主动的“预判式”服务。至于 iOS 预览版和 Mac 完整早期体验之间的能力差距，Snap 同样没有公开细节。

从应用场景看，Specs Intelligence 瞄准的是工作流管理、个人事务协调、旅行信息整合以及 AR 眼镜上的免手操作信息呈现。它试图把分散在邮件、聊天、日历等账户中的信息统一起来，形成跨设备的个人上下文，并在用户尚未明确提问时主动推送建议。这种模式如果成功，可能让 AI 助手从“问答工具”进一步演变为“持续运行的个人代理”。

但真正的挑战在于隐私和信任。Specs Intelligence 需要用户授权连接大量敏感账户，并让 Snap 处理这些数据。为了缓解担忧，Snap 表示，它无法查看或访问用户与 Specs Intelligence 一起使用的个人内容，并且“来自连接账户的个人内容不会被用于训练或微调 Snap 的 AI 模型，也不会用于提供个性化广告”。不过，这仍然是一个很高的门槛，尤其考虑到此前其他拥有广泛数据访问权限的 AI 助手已经让不少用户感到不安。Specs Intelligence 能否成立，不仅取决于其预判和主动服务是否真正有用，也取决于 Snap 能否在功能价值与隐私信任之间建立足够稳固的平衡。
